The '''Armenian Mathematical Union''' or '''AMU''' (Armenian: {{lang|hy|Հայկական Մաթեմատիկական Միություն}}, '''ՀՄՄ'''{{r|statutes}}) is a [[mathematical society]] founded in [[Armenia]] in 1991.
The AMU is based in [[Yerevan]], and has been a member of the [[European Mathematical Society]] since 2016.{{r|ems1|ems2}} It is recognised by the [[International Mathematics Union]] as the official mathematical society of Armenia.{{r|imu}}

==History==
The first association of Armenian mathematicians was formed in 1920, during the [[First Armenian Republic]]; its president was Ervand Kogbetlianz, a professor at [[Yerevan State University]].{{r|ems2}}
The modern Armenian Mathematical Union was founded in 1991, the same year that Armenia gained independence due to the [[dissolution of the USSR]].{{r|ems2}}
In 2020 the AMU dedicated its annual session to the 100th anniversary of the first association.{{r|session}}

==Activities and awards==
The AMU has organised several international conferences.{{r|ems1}} In May–June 2018 it hosted a conference to celebrate the 120th anniversary of [[Emil Artin]]'s birth.{{r|ysu1}}

Since 2001 the AMU has annually awarded the [[Emil Artin Junior Prize in Mathematics]] to a mathematician under the age of thirty-five who studied in Armenia, for "outstanding contributions in algebra, geometry, topology, and number theory."{{r|ems2}} The prize is named after Emil Artin. The winner is announced in the ''[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]'', and as of 2024 receives a cash prize of US$1400.{{r|ems2|prize2024}}

==Presidents==
The Armenian Mathematical Union has had 7 presidents since its founding.{{r|mactutor}}
* Alexander Talalyan (1991–1994)
* Norayr Arakelian (1994–1997)
* [[Rouben V. Ambartzumian|Ruben Ambartzumian]] (1997–2001)
* {{ill|Norayr Yengibaryan|hy|Նորայր Ենգիբարյան}} (2001–2004)
* Hrachik Hayrapetyan (2004–2011)
* Tigran Harutunyan (2011–2017)
* Yuri Movsisyan (2017–present)
